title: Corpus backup has two copies on one site; the off-site leg is built and needs one approval (destination)
evidence:
The single-copy risk is CLOSED: bin/corpus_backup.sh keeps a verified second copy of the render corpus at <repo>/corpus-backup/ on the local NVMe, nightly via Hermes cron bae1bd85ec35 (first snapshot 59,704 files / 83.02 GB; DB check verified 171 resolvable corpus file(s), missing=0). OFF-SITE is the remaining bar: the NAS and this box are in the same place, so one fire, flood or theft takes both copies at once. Two independent devices is met; off-site is the next bar and is deliberately not claimed as done.

CORRECTED 2026-09-21 -- this is no longer an unobtainable-credential ask. The app keys stay dead (the key in .env and the one in Rails credentials are the same id, 00437451bb92cd0000000000e: aws s3 ls on fluffy-train-development/-production -> InvalidAccessKeyId; Rails' own b2 service.exist? -> Forbidden; nothing written to B2 since 2026-05-28). But the open claim that "no agent can obtain those from here" was WRONG about this box: ~/.aws/credentials carries the profile `b2_tim`, a LIVE key for the SAME B2 account -- `aws s3 ls --profile b2_tim --endpoint-url https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com` returns 6 buckets with rc=0 and `aws s3api head-bucket --bucket tim-training-data` returns rc=0. Every sibling project already has a prefix under `tim-training-data/` (BreastTissue-Net, crawlr, dino-x, eidolon, eros, ffhq, flenwheel, flux2-lora, gpt-oss-20b-eros, jubilant-palm-tree, leica-look, loras, outputs, processed, prx-tg, stratum-api, therapist-in-a-minor, turbo-octo-funicular); turbo-carnival has none, and no object in B2 matches carnival/corpus/sarah/comfyui. The NAS-side Synology buckets are not covering it either (tim-synology-cloudsync/@SynologyCloudSync/ and /photos/ hold only the 2025-05-13 markers).

THE OFF-SITE LEG IS BUILT AND VERIFIED IN-REPO: `bin/corpus_backup.sh --offsite [--dry-run]`, or `CORPUS_BACKUP_OFFSITE=1` on the nightly run. It packages the DB-defined corpus (171 resolvable photos.path files + the 339-row manifest) as one tar.gz, uploads to s3://tim-training-data/turbo-carnival/corpus/, then reads the object back and compares ContentLength and the sha256 metadata -- an upload nobody read back is a claim, not a copy. Destination/profile/prefix/endpoint are overridable (CORPUS_BACKUP_BUCKET / _PROFILE / _PREFIX / _ENDPOINT). DEFAULT OFF, because it writes into Tim's B2 account.

WHAT IS NEEDED FROM TIM: approve the destination (default s3://tim-training-data/turbo-carnival/corpus/) or name another S3-compatible target. That is the whole ask -- one yes/no. On approval the wiring is the env var CORPUS_BACKUP_OFFSITE=1 in the tc-corpus-backup tick and nothing else. Scope stays the publishable corpus (~176 MiB); the ~83 GB historical sarah1a3 tree stays on the two local copies, because off-siting it is a recurring-cost decision and it recovers nothing the app published.

Second half, unchanged and still Tim's file rather than this repo's: /home/tim/backup.sh:27 rsyncs /mnt/fscache/essdee/ with -x and no --copy-links, so ComfyUI/output mirrors as a dangling symlink onto the same NAS volume -- the nightly backup still looks like it covers the images while covering none of them.
